page: Microsoft Azure D128s_v6 is a Dsv6-family virtual machine configured with 128 dedicated vCPUs and 512.0 GB of RAM, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The underlying hardware features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, consisting of 64 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for remote disk attachment.

Benchmark data reveals a performance profile characterized by top-tier multi-core capabilities alongside average single-core performance. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance is in the middle 50 percent, whereas multi-core CPU performance reaches the top 25 percent. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached bandwidth and large block uncached read bandwidth both placing in the top 10 percent. Multi-threaded operations scale effectively, as demonstrated by top-tier results in bzip3 multi-threaded decompression and Geekbench multi-core scoring. However, single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression remain in the average tier.

The server demonstrates strong performance in specialized computational tasks, achieving top-tier results in Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations. It also displays top-tier throughput for static web serving and strong to top-tier LLM inference speeds, processing 41.27 tokens per second for large 70B model prompts. Given the high vCPU density and balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core, the D128s_v6 offers qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads that can leverage its multi-threaded capacity and advanced vector instructions. It is suited for large-scale database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
